core_obligations: Fibre bound: limit-dimension lets one assume all fibres of f_0 have dimension <= d.

Constructible locus: the locus where the fibre dimension is <= d-1 is open and retrocompact (openness lemma); its complement E is constructible and contains the image of X -> X_0 (dimension-fibre-after-base-change).
Containment and conclusion: limit-contained-in-constructible puts the images of X_i -> X_0 inside E for i large; the base-change lemma then gives all fibres of X_i -> Y_i dimension exactly d.
proof_roadmap: Open locus, constructible complement, image containment.
Eventual containment; base-change lemma restores dimension d.
difficulty_reason: limit-dimension bounds the fibres; openness of the bounded-dimension locus (retrocompact) gives a constructible complement E; the image containment via dimension-fibre-after-base-change plus limit-contained-in-constructible; the same base-change lemma restores dimension exactly d. Multi-engine assembly.

compared.difference: The sibling is the <= d bound version, proved in the source by a one-line citation of limit-dimension (not carded); this lemma is the exact-d version with the constructible-locus work. Different statements.
